results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Rising Waters.
results.text:
I built a Blue-Green "Rising Waters Prison" brew. The validator accepted it as legal with no warnings.

**The plan**
Rising Waters (3U) says lands don't untap normally, and each player untaps just one land in their upkeep. It does nothing to creatures or artifacts. So the deck makes its mana from 12 mana creatures and Mox Diamond, locks the opponent onto one land a turn, and attacks with cheap creatures. Opposition then taps down their last land and their blockers.

**Deck (60)**
- **Mana creatures (12):** 4 Birds of Paradise, 4 Llanowar Elves, 4 Fyndhorn Elves
- **Other creatures (7):** 3 Quirion Ranger, 4 River Boa
- **Threats:** 3 Call of the Herd
- **Lock (9):** 4 Rising Waters, 2 Winter Orb, 3 Opposition
- **Counters and card draw (10):** 4 Daze, 4 Mana Leak, 2 Gush
- **Mana rock:** 1 Mox Diamond
- **Lands (18):** 8 Forest, 7 Island, 1 Yavimaya Coast, 2 Rishadan Port

**Why these cards**
- **Getting around your own lock:**
  - **Quirion Ranger:** returns a Forest to your hand to untap a creature. Return a tapped Forest, replay it untapped, and you've gained a mana *and* untapped an elf.
  - **Daze and Gush:** their free costs return Islands to your hand, so a tapped Island comes back untapped. Under the lock, these free spells cost you nothing.
- **Extra lock pieces:**
  - **Winter Orb:** a 2-mana second copy of the lock. It also limits lands only, so your creatures are unaffected.
  - **Rishadan Port:** can tap the one land the opponent just untapped.
- **Odds:** you have a 64% chance to see one of the 6 lock pieces by turn 3 on the play, and 89% to see a mana creature by then.
- **Finishers:**
  - **River Boa:** can't be blocked by blue decks and regenerates using elf mana.
  - **Call of the Herd:** two 3/3s from one card.
  - **Mana Leak:** asks for 3 more mana, which an opponent on one land a turn can almost never pay.

**The mana**
I kept it lean on purpose: 18 lands plus 13 non-land mana sources, with an average mana value of 2.14. The check tool suggests about 21 lands, and real Cradle Control lists run about 21 green sources (this deck has 16). Under your own Rising Waters, extra lands help less than mana creatures do. I cut Counterspell because 11 blue sources can't reliably make UU.

**Sideboard (15)**
- **Blue decks (Stiflenought, UB Psychatog, Replenish, Standstill):** bring in 3 Choke. Their Islands then never untap normally, and with Rising Waters they get just one land back a turn. Add 2 Tormod's Crypt against Replenish and Psychatog.
- **Sligh and Goblins:** bring in 3 Hydroblast, 2 Masticore and 1 Wall of Roots. Cut Winter Orb and Gush. Rising Waters is at its weakest against cheap red decks, so lean on Opposition and blockers.
- **Enchantress:** bring in 2 Annul and 2 Naturalize. The lock starves their expensive enchantments.
- **Terrageddon:** their Armageddon barely hurts you because your mana comes from creatures. Keep Opposition in for their creatures.
- **Hermit Druid Combo:** bring in Tormod's Crypt.

**Things to know**
This is a **brew**. Rising Waters shows up in 0 recent lists, so it has never been tested in tournaments. I took the mana-creature base and Opposition/Winter Orb idea from Cradle Control, and the free counterspells (Daze, Gush) from Stasis decks. Two risks:
- Hibernation and creature sweepers return or wipe your mana creatures, leaving you stuck under your own lock. Hibernation is a small sideboard card in Stiflenought and Stasis lists.
- Fast red starts (Sligh) are the toughest matchup.

The 7-turn kill estimate is my guess, not something I tested.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Mind Over Matter.
results.text:
I built a mono-blue Mind Over Matter ramp-combo deck. It's a **brew**: the tournament data shows only one Mind Over Matter list in the last 90 days, and the reference Rogue list I pulled was an unrelated deck, so nothing proven exists to copy. I borrowed the general approach of the big-mana blue combo decks (Dream Halls, Frantic Storm) for the mana base, card draw and counterspells.

**The plan**
Ramp with Mind Stone, Thran Dynamo and Ancient Tomb, and protect yourself with counterspells. Then land Mind Over Matter ("Discard a card: You may tap or untap target artifact, creature, or land"). From then on, every card in your hand is mana or more cards. You win by having an opponent draw more cards than they have left with Stroke of Genius.

**Main deck (60)**
- **The combo (11):** 4 Mind Over Matter, 2 Arcanis the Omnipotent, 4 Stroke of Genius, 1 Morphling
- **Ramp (7):** 4 Thran Dynamo, 3 Mind Stone
- **Counterspells and removal (9):** 4 Counterspell, 3 Mana Leak, 2 Powder Keg
- **Card draw and selection (12):** 4 Impulse, 2 Opt, 2 Intuition, 2 Fact or Fiction, 2 Deep Analysis
- **Lands (21):** 18 Island, 3 Ancient Tomb

**Sideboard (15)**
3 Hydroblast, 2 Chill, 1 Powder Keg, 3 Annul, 2 Tormod's Crypt, 2 Stifle, 1 Hibernation, 1 Rushing River

**How it wins**
- **Thran Dynamo** taps for 3. With Mind Over Matter out, each card you discard to untap it is worth 3 mana. Untapping Ancient Tomb gets you 2 (but it deals 2 damage to you each time).
- **Arcanis loop:** Arcanis taps to draw 3. Discard 1 to untap Arcanis and 2 to untap Dynamo. Each loop nets 6 mana without using up your hand, until you've drawn your whole library.
- **Without Arcanis:** cast Stroke of Genius on yourself. X cards turn into about 3X mana through Dynamo, so each Stroke pays for a bigger one. Then aim the last Stroke at your opponent with X bigger than their library. They lose when they try to draw from an empty library.
- **Deep Analysis** is extra fuel: discard it to Mind Over Matter, then flash it back from the graveyard for {1}{U} and 3 life.
- **Mind Over Matter is also defense:** you can discard to tap down an attacker or tap an opponent's land during their upkeep.

**Why these cards**
- 2 Intuition help find Mind Over Matter. Searching for three copies guarantees you get one.
- Morphling is a backup win if your Strokes get countered.
- I kept Arcanis at 2 because it's a legendary 6-drop. Extra copies would just be discard fodder.

**The mana**
- 18 Islands supply the {U}{U}{U}{U} that Mind Over Matter costs.
- check_deck suggested about 23.7 lands. I run 21, plus 7 mana artifacts, which comes to 28 mana sources. Flooding is fine here because extra lands become fuel.
- The checker found no errors or warnings and no problems compared with Dream Halls lists.
- Odds without a mulligan:
  - Seeing a Mind Over Matter by turn 5: 56.6%. Impulse, Opt, Intuition and Fact or Fiction push that higher, but I didn't calculate by how much.
  - Seeing a fast-mana piece by turn 5: 89.1%.
  - Having both Mind Over Matter and a Stroke or Arcanis by turn 7: about 49%.
- Realistic kill turn: 6–7.

**Sideboarding against the current field**
- **Sligh (9.9%) and Goblins (4.4%):** bring in 3 Hydroblast, 2 Chill and the third Powder Keg. Take out Deep Analysis, Morphling and Opt.
- **Enchantress (12.5%):** bring in 3 Annul and Hibernation. Cut Powder Keg.
- **Hermit Druid (5.5%) and Replenish (4.8%):** bring in 2 Tormod's Crypt, 2 Stifle and Annul. Stifle counters Hermit Druid's activated ability.
- **Terrageddon (11.2%):** keep in your counterspells for Armageddon. Bring in Hibernation for their green threats and Stifle.
- **Stiflenought (10.4%) and Psychatog (4.8%):** these are counterspell matchups. Bring in Stifle and Rushing River, and wait to resolve Mind Over Matter until you have backup counterspells. Watch out for their Back to Basics, which shuts down Ancient Tomb.

**Not verified**
- I haven't tested how this performs against the field. It has no tournament results behind it.

I built a mono-black "Ritual Processor" deck. It's a brew: Phyrexian Processor shows up in only 4 Premodern lists from the last 90 days (0.2% share), mostly in Devourer Combo sideboards, so there was no proven Processor deck to copy.

**The plan**
Fast black mana gets Processor down on turn 1 or 2. Discard spells clear out answers first, and edicts and removal clear the way for the huge Minion token. The best opening is Swamp → Dark Ritual → Lotus Petal → Processor on turn 1. Another is Ancient Tomb on turn 1, then Swamp and Ritual on turn 2 for 5 mana. Processor is an artifact, not a creature, so you can make a token the same turn if you have 8 mana. Phyrexian Negator, Hypnotic Specter and Masticore are backup threats in the Suicide Black style, so the deck can still win when Processor doesn't show up.

**Main deck (60)**
- **Processor and mana:**
  - 4 Phyrexian Processor
  - 4 Dark Ritual
  - 4 Lotus Petal
- **Discard:**
  - 4 Duress
  - 4 Cabal Therapy
  - 2 Unmask
- **Other threats:**
  - 4 Phyrexian Negator
  - 4 Hypnotic Specter
  - 2 Masticore
- **Removal:**
  - 3 Smother
  - 3 Diabolic Edict
  - 1 Snuff Out
- **Lands (21):**
  - 13 Swamp
  - 4 Ancient Tomb
  - 2 City of Traitors
  - 2 Mishra's Factory

**Why these cards**
- **Fast mana:** Ritual, Petal, Tomb and City (14 cards) let you cast Processor early and still have mana for its 4-mana activation. Black has no good way to search for it: Demonic Tutor isn't legal in Premodern, Vampiric Tutor is banned, and the legal tutors are slow.
- **Discard (10 cards):** Duress, Therapy and Unmask take away artifact removal and counterspells before you risk your life total. Unmask can be cast for free by exiling a black card from your hand.
- **Edicts and removal:** They clear blockers. Smother also kills Phyrexian Dreadnought, since its mana value is 1, which matters against Stiflenought.
- **How much life to pay:** About 5–6 against Sligh and Goblins, where your life total is under pressure. About 8–10 against Enchantress, Psychatog and combo decks. Remember Ancient Tomb deals 2 damage to you each time you tap it.

**The odds (no mulligans, on the play)**
- About a 49% chance to have Processor by turn 3.
- About a 79% chance to have Processor, Negator or Masticore by turn 2.
- That's why the backup threats are there.

**The mana**
The mana borrows from Moneyball Black: 17 black sources, the same as Moneyball's average. The deck checker flagged that I run 21 lands where Moneyball averages 23. I kept it at 21 on purpose: 4 Petals, 4 Rituals and two lands that tap for 2 (Tomb and City) give 29 cards that make mana. Play City of Traitors after your other land drops, because playing another land sacrifices it.

**Sideboard (15) and how to use it**
- **Enchantress and Terrageddon:** bring in 3 Dystopia and 2 Gloom (Gloom only hits white spells). Discard is already strong here, and Processor survives Armageddon.
- **Sligh and Goblins:** bring in 3 Engineered Plague and 2 Powder Keg. Pay less life. Take out Unmask and some Specters.
- **Stiflenought:** bring in 2 Snuff Out and the Powder Kegs.
- **Hermit Druid and Replenish:** bring in 3 Tormod's Crypt. Keep all the discard.
- **Psychatog:** keep all the discard and bring in the extra Snuff Outs.

**What I couldn't check**
These matchup notes are my judgment. Nobody has posted results for this deck, so none of it has been tested in real play.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Volrath's Shapeshifter and Phage the Untouchable.
results.text:
Now let me check the draft.

I've built a blue-green brew with no black mana. Phage is never cast; it's only there to be discarded so Volrath's Shapeshifter can copy it.

**The plan**
Shapeshifter (1UU, a 0/1) has the full text of the top card of your graveyard whenever that card is a creature. With Phage on top, Shapeshifter becomes a 4/4. It destroys any creature it deals combat damage to, and a player it deals combat damage to loses the game. Shapeshifter never "enters" as Phage, so Phage's "you lose the game" enter trigger never happens.

The deck plays Shapeshifter early as a harmless 0/1 so it can attack later. On the turn you attack, you discard Phage at instant speed and swing. The fastest start is Birds on turn 1, Shapeshifter on turn 2, then Survival or a Mongrel, which can win as early as turn 3–4.

**Key rules points (from the card text)**
- **Use abilities, not spells, to discard Phage.** Any instant or sorcery you cast goes to the graveyard *after* it resolves, landing on top of Phage. That's why there's no Careful Study, Entomb or fetchlands. The discard engines are all abilities:
  - **Wild Mongrel:** discarding is free.
  - **Aquamoeba:** discarding is free.
  - **Merfolk Looter:** tap to draw, then discard.
  - **Survival of the Fittest:** {G}, discard a creature card: put any creature from your library into your hand.
  - **Shapeshifter itself:** {2}: discard a card.
- **Survival does double duty.** Discard anything to fetch Phage, then discard Phage to fetch whatever else you need. It also finds a missing Shapeshifter.
- **Intuition:** name three Phages. One goes to your hand to discard; the other two go to your graveyard.
- **Wonder and Brawn work from anywhere in the graveyard.** With an Island, Wonder gives your creatures flying. With a Forest, Brawn gives them trample. A flying Phage gets past ground blockers.
- **Wait to discard Phage.** If Pyroclasm comes at a 0/1 Shapeshifter, discard Phage with Mongrel in response and it survives as a 4/4.
- **Don't run two Shapeshifters as Phage at once.** Phage is legendary, so the legend rule makes you lose one.
- **Never reanimate Phage.** That's why the deck has no Animate Dead or Exhume.

**Odds (no mulligans, on the play, by turn 4)**
- About 86% to see a Shapeshifter, Survival or Intuition.
- About 97% to see a discard outlet.
- About 83% to have both.
- A natural Shapeshifter alone is only about 53%, which is why the tutors matter.

**Mana**
21 lands: 4 Yavimaya Coast, 9 Island and 8 Forest, plus 4 Birds. That's 15 blue and 14 green sources, in line with real UG Madness lists. There are no fetchlands because a sacrificed fetchland would land on top of Phage. check_deck warns that Phage has no black sources; that's on purpose, since you never cast it.

**Sideboarding against the current top decks**
- **Enchantress (12.5%):** bring in 2 Tranquil Domain, 2 Naturalize and 3 Annul to deal with Parallax Wave and Elephant Grass. Wonder already gets you past ground blockers.
- **Terrageddon (11.2%):** bring in 2 Mana Leak to back up the Counterspells and Dazes against Armageddon. Hold Phage in hand until you're ready, so Pyroclasm only kills a 0/1.
- **Stiflenought (10.4%):** bring in Annul to counter Phyrexian Dreadnought, Hydroblast for their red cards, and Uktabi Orangutan, which Survival can fetch. Gilded Drake (main deck) steals the Dreadnought.
- **Sligh and Goblins:** bring in 3 Hydroblast. Take out Daze and the Intuitions.
- **Hermit Druid, Replenish and Psychatog:** bring in 2 Tormod's Crypt. Only use it at a moment when your own graveyard doesn't matter, because it exiles one player's whole graveyard.

**Label and caveats**
This is a **brew**. It borrows its mana and counterspell base from UG Madness. Phage has no tournament results in the last 90 days, and Shapeshifter shows up almost only in Hermit Druid Combo. I haven't playtested it. Its weak points are graveyard hate (in the field, Tormod's Crypt is in about 45% of lists over the last 90 days) and removal used after Shapeshifter becomes Phage. Keep an outlet ready to discard another creature in response.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Seismic Assault.
results.text:
I submitted this as **Seismic Lands**, a red-green Premodern brew. The tools show Seismic Assault in only one list in the last 90 days, a Dream Halls deck, so nobody has a proven version of this plan. I borrowed the land base and land-matters ideas from Terrageddon, which is 11.2% of the current field.

**The plan:** Play a lot of lands, put even more of them in your hand, and turn each one into 2 damage with Seismic Assault. Early on you trade burn for the opponent's creatures. Then Terravore gets huge from all the discarded lands, and Groundskeeper keeps returning the same basic land so you can throw it again for 2 damage every turn.

**Main deck (60)**
- 4 Seismic Assault, 4 Mox Diamond, 4 Sylvan Library, 4 Mulch, 4 Lightning Bolt, 3 Gamble
- 4 Terravore, 4 Wild Mongrel, 3 Groundskeeper, 1 Harvest Wurm
- 25 lands: 7 Mountain, 4 Forest, 4 Wooded Foothills, 4 Karplusan Forest, 2 Gemstone Mine, 2 Forgotten Cave, 1 Tranquil Thicket, 1 Treetop Village

**Why these cards**
- **Mox Diamond:** You pay for it by discarding a land, which already grows Terravore. It also lets you cast Seismic Assault ({R}{R}{R}) on turn 2.
- **Mulch:** Puts every land in your top four cards into your hand and the rest into the graveyard. In this deck that's both more burn and more Terravore power.
- **Sylvan Library:** Lets you look at extra cards each turn and keep the ones you want.
- **Groundskeeper and Harvest Wurm:** Each returns a basic land from your graveyard to your hand. Groundskeeper does it for {1}{G}, as often as you can pay, so with Seismic Assault out it's a repeatable 2 damage. That's why the deck runs 15 basic lands.
- **Wild Mongrel:** Another way to discard spare cards, including lands for Terravore.
- **The cycling lands:** Forgotten Cave and Tranquil Thicket can be cycled to draw a card when Seismic Assault isn't out.
- **Gamble:** It searches your library for any card, so it's effectively Seismic copies 5 to 7. The calculator puts the odds of seeing Seismic Assault or Gamble by turn 4 at 74.1%, up from 52.8% with Seismic alone (no mulligans counted). Gamble then discards a card at random. In a hand this full of lands, that's usually a land, which feeds Terravore.

**Mana:** 25 lands plus 4 Mox Diamond, close to Terrageddon's average of about 26 lands. That's more than a normal deck because lands are your ammunition. The deck has 23 red sources for {R}{R}{R} and 20 green for Terravore's {G}{G}. The deck checker flagged that the deck has far fewer white sources than Terrageddon. That doesn't matter because this deck has no white cards.

**Sideboard (15):** 2 Pyroblast, 2 Red Elemental Blast, 3 Naturalize, 2 Tormod's Crypt, 2 Pyroclasm, 2 Anarchy, 2 Zuran Orb
- **Blue decks (Stiflenought, UB Psychatog, Standstill, Replenish):** Bring in Pyroblast and Red Elemental Blast for Harvest Wurm and some Bolts.
- **Enchantress (the top deck at 12.5%):** Bring in Naturalize and Anarchy (which destroys all white permanents) for creatures that can't get through. Your burn mostly goes at their face.
- **Hermit Druid and Replenish:** Bring in Tormod's Crypt. Against Replenish, add Naturalize too.
- **Sligh and Goblins:** Bring in Pyroclasm. Zuran Orb turns your extra lands into life. Mongrels and Groundskeepers should mostly survive Pyroclasm, since Mongrel can pump and Groundskeeper is cheap. Terravore will usually be bigger than 2/2.
- **Terrageddon:** Armageddon hurts them more than you, as long as you've kept lands in hand to throw. Zuran Orb helps here.

**What I couldn't verify:** This deck has never been tested in a tournament, so treat these numbers as a starting point. Things to watch:
- Groundskeeper is weak when you draw it without Seismic Assault out.
- Gamble can occasionally discard the card you just found.

If you're flooding, cut 1 land. If the deck runs out of gas, add a second Harvest Wurm.

results.prompt: Brew me a mono-green Premodern ramp deck built around Rofellos, Llanowar Emissary.
results.text:
I built a mono-green Rofellos ramp deck and submitted it. It's a **brew**: Rofellos shows up in 0 recent Premodern lists, so there was no proven version to copy. I borrowed the dork package and land count from Premodern Elves, but left out its Survival of the Fittest engine and its off-color splashes so it stays a Forest-ramp deck.

**The plan**
Play an Elf on turn 1 and Rofellos on turn 2. From turn 3 on, Rofellos makes one green mana per Forest, often 4–6 or more. Spend that on Plow Under to hold the opponent's lands back, then win with Deranged Hermit squirrels, Masticore, a Kamahl team pump, or a huge Hurricane.

**Main deck (60)**
- **Mana creatures (17):** 4 Llanowar Elves, 4 Fyndhorn Elves, 4 Rofellos, 3 Quirion Ranger, 2 Priest of Titania
- **Ramp and value (6):** 3 Wood Elves, 2 Multani's Acolyte, 1 Krosan Tusker
- **Threats and answers (8):** 3 Deranged Hermit, 2 Masticore, 1 Kamahl, Fist of Krosa, 1 Silvos, Rogue Elemental, 1 Nantuko Vigilante
- **Spells (9):** 2 Worldly Tutor, 2 Sylvan Library, 3 Plow Under, 2 Hurricane
- **Lands (20):** 17 Forest, 3 Gaea's Cradle

**Why these cards**
- **Quirion Ranger:** Its cost is returning a Forest to your hand, and it untaps a creature. Untapping Rofellos gets you a second activation; you lose one Forest from his count, then replay it as your land drop.
- **Wood Elves and Krosan Tusker:** Wood Elves puts a Forest onto the battlefield untapped, so with Rofellos out it pays for itself right away. Tusker cycles to fetch a basic land, or comes down as a 6/5 late.
- **Worldly Tutor and Sylvan Library:** These help find Rofellos. The odds of seeing Rofellos or a Worldly Tutor by turn 3 on the play are 64%. Library also lets you dig for answers.
- **Priest of Titania:** A second big-mana creature so the deck still works when Rofellos is dead or not drawn.
- **Finishers:** Masticore's {2} abilities (ping a creature, regenerate) soak up spare mana. Deranged Hermit's 5-mana echo is easy to pay. Kamahl gives the team +3/+3 and trample, and Silvos regenerates for {G}.
- **Hurricane:** It also deals X damage to you, so cast it when you're ahead on life or it's exactly lethal.

**The mana**
Rofellos counts Forests, so the lands are all basic Forests plus 3 Gaea's Cradle, with no fetchlands or duals. Cradle isn't a Forest, but it taps for one green per creature you control. check_deck passed with no warnings. It suggested about 20.3 lands; real Elves lists average 19, and I run 20 because the top of the curve is higher.

**Sideboard (15) and how to use it**
- **Sligh and Goblins:** +2 Ravenous Baloth, +2 Spike Feeder. Take out Sylvan Library, Plow Under and Hurricane.
- **Enchantress (the most-played deck, 12.5%):** +2 Tranquil Domain, +2 Naturalize, +3 Xantid Swarm. Plow Under stays in; take out Masticore and Hurricane.
- **Stiflenought:** +2 Uktabi Orangutan, because Phyrexian Dreadnought is an artifact creature. Take out a Hurricane and an Acolyte.
- **Hermit Druid Combo, Replenish, Psychatog:** +2 Tormod's Crypt and +3 Xantid Swarm (it stops them casting spells when it attacks). Take out slow cards like Silvos and Tusker.
- **Terrageddon:** Armageddon is a real problem for a mana-creature deck. Leave Plow Under in, apply pressure early, and don't overextend your lands.

**What I couldn't verify**
There's no tournament data for this deck, so the matchup plans above are reasoned from what the cards do, not from results. The deck's main weakness is sweepers and removal aimed at Rofellos. Priest of Titania and Gaea's Cradle are the backup when that happens.

results.prompt: Brew me a Legacy deck built around Thassa's Oracle and Tainted Pact.
results.text:
I built a **brew**: a singleton-style Dimir (blue-black) Oracle-Pact combo deck. Legacy has no proven list for these two cards. Tainted Pact shows up in just one "Rogue" list in the last 90 days. Thassa's Oracle mostly appears in Doomsday decks (255 lists), and Doomsday plays 4-ofs that would break Pact. Demonic Consultation, the usual partner for Oracle, is banned in Legacy, so Pact has to do that job.

**The plan**
- Cast Thassa's Oracle and let it resolve. With its enter trigger on the stack, cast Tainted Pact and never take a card.
- Pact keeps exiling until it hits a second card with the same name. No name in this library appears twice, so it exiles the whole library. The trigger then sees devotion 2 against 0 cards left, and you win.
- The trigger still wins if they kill Oracle in response, because 0 is at least 0.
- It costs 4 mana and both pieces are instants or at least work at instant speed around the trigger, so you're aiming to win on turn 3–4 behind protection.

**Why the key cards**

- **Other artifacts:** 1 Pithing Needle, 2 Lotus Petal
- **Tutors:** 4 Trinket Mage, 2 Enlightened Tutor
- **Card selection:** 4 Brainstorm, 4 Ponder, 1 Lórien Revealed

Get Salvagers onto the battlefield with Lion's Eye Diamond (LED) available, then loop them for as much mana as you want, and win with Walking Ballista.

The loop works like this:
1. Sacrifice LED (this discards your hand) for three white mana.
2. Pay {1}{W} to have Salvagers return LED to your hand.
3. Cast LED again for 0.
4. Each loop leaves you one extra mana, and you can choose any color.

- 19 lands, with 17.5 white and 14.5 blue sources by the checker's count. That's the land count the deck checker recommended.

- **Ocelot Aggro, Eldrazi Aggro:** bring in Solitude, Engineered Explosives and Ensnaring Bridge. Salvagers can also rebuy Explosives, which has mana value 0 in the graveyard.
- **Tron, Lands:** bring in the second Pithing Needle, plus Force of Negation.

I built **Temur Hypergenesis**, a brew that cascades into a free Hypergenesis on turn 1–2.

**The plan**
Hypergenesis has no mana cost, and the deck plays no other nonland card that costs less than 3. So every Shardless Agent or Violent Outburst you cast always flips Hypergenesis and casts it for free.
- You put things onto the battlefield first, so you empty your hand of fatties. Opponents get to put cards down too, but most Legacy hands have little worth putting in.
- Violent Outburst is an instant, so you can cascade at the end of the opponent's turn and untap with the board.
- Show and Tell is a second way to cheat fatties in. It can't be cascaded into, so it's pure backup.
- Force of Will and Force of Negation protect the combo for free.

**Key cards**
- **Shardless Agent and Violent Outburst (4 each):** the eight cascade spells. You have about a 75% chance to see one by turn 2 on the draw.
- **Fast mana:** Elvish Spirit Guide (4), Simian Spirit Guide (3) and Ancient Tomb (3). Tomb plus both guides casts Outburst on turn 1. Tomb plus any land plus one guide does it on turn 2.
- **Elesh Norn, Mother of Machines:** put it down first in the Hypergenesis loop. The opponent's enter triggers then don't happen, and yours trigger twice (two Archon triggers, two Atraxa reveals).
- **The other fatties:**
  - Archon of Cruelty: makes them sacrifice a creature, discard and lose life, and you draw.
  - Atraxa, Grand Unifier: refills your hand.
  - Emrakul and Progenitus: very hard to answer.
  - Terastodon: destroys three of their lands or other noncreature permanents.
  - Inkwell Leviathan: has shroud.
  - Griselbrand: draw seven cards.
  
  Their colors don't matter, because you never cast them.
- **Blue cards for Force of Will:** there are 18 (Agents, Show and Tell, the Forces, Atraxa, Leviathan).
- **Fury and Endurance:** free answers to Ocelot Aggro and Eldrazi Aggro, which together are about 15% of the field.

Odds of having a cascade spell or Show and Tell **and** a fatty by turn 3 on the play: about 76%.

**Mana**
16 lands plus 7 spirit guides. I borrowed the fetch-and-dual base from Living End lists and added Ancient Tomb for speed.
- Blue: 10 sources by the checker's count, about 11 counting that Wooded Foothills can fetch Volcanic or Tropical Island. Living End lists run about 12.6. I accepted that because you rarely hard-cast blue cards.
- The checker warned about 0 white and 0 black sources for Progenitus and Griselbrand. You can ignore that: they only ever come in through Hypergenesis or Show and Tell.
- **Rules to follow:** never add a nonland card that costs less than 3, main deck or sideboard, or cascades will hit it instead of Hypergenesis. That rules out Lotus Petal, Pyroblast and Inevitable Betrayal.

**Sideboarding**
- **Dimir Tempo, Izzet Tempo, Doomsday, OmniTell:** bring in 3 Mystical Dispute and 2 Subtlety. Take out Fury, Endurance and the clunkiest fatty.
- **Reanimator, Hogaak:** bring in 3 Leyline of the Void (free in your opening hand) and the second Endurance. Subtlety is also good against Reanimator.
- **Ocelot Aggro, Eldrazi Aggro, Death and Taxes:** bring in the last 2 Fury. Take out Force of Negation.
- **Tron, Lands:** bring in 2 Magus of the Moon and 2 Force of Vigor (also good against artifact and enchantment hate). Take out Fury.

This is a **brew**: Hypergenesis shows 0 lists in the last 90 days of results. The cascade and Force shell is borrowed from Living End.
- Hypergenesis is symmetrical, so an opponent holding their own fatties or hate permanents can benefit too. Norn first limits the damage.
- Two interactions come from my rules knowledge, not from the tools:
  - Cascade lets you cast the sorcery during the opponent's end step.
  - Trinisphere would tax the free cascade spells. That's why it isn't in the deck.

**The plan**
Ramp to 6–7 lands with cheap green spells, guard the key turn with Force of Will, then cast Scapeshift.
- **With Prismatic Omen (or Dryad of the Ilysian Grove) in play:** every land you control is a Mountain, Valakut included. Sacrifice 6 lands and fetch Valakut plus 5 others. Each one enters as a Mountain while 5 other Mountains are there, so you get 6 triggers × 3 damage = 18.

The deck aims to win on turn 5.

- 4 Scapeshift
- 3 Prismatic Omen
- 2 Dryad of the Ilysian Grove
- 1 Primeval Titan
- 1 Summoner's Pact
- 2 Uro, Titan of Nature's Wrath
- 4 Three Visits
- 4 Growth Spiral
- 4 Brainstorm
- 4 Ponder

- **Three Visits:** it fetches a Forest *card* onto the battlefield untapped. Taiga and Tropical Island count, so it's both ramp and color fixing. Taiga is also a Mountain for Valakut.
- **Growth Spiral and Uro:** they ramp, draw cards, and are blue cards you can exile to Force of Will. Uro's life gain also helps against aggro.
- **Summoner's Pact:** finds Dryad, Primeval Titan or Uro. You must pay {2}{G}{G} at your next upkeep or you lose the game.
- **Primeval Titan:** fetches Valakut plus a Mountain when it enters and every time it attacks. It's the backup win if Scapeshift gets countered.
- **Brainstorm, Ponder, 4 Force of Will and 2 Force of Negation:** the standard Legacy blue package, taken from Beanstalk Control. The deck has 20 blue cards to exile to the Forces.

- **25 lands, on purpose.** The checker compared this to Beanstalk Control's 20.4 lands and said to cut about 5. I'm ignoring that because this deck has to put 6–7 lands into play.

|---|---|
| Dimir Tempo / Izzet Tempo | 2 Pyroblast, 2 Carpet of Flowers, 2 Veil of Summer (lets Scapeshift resolve through counterspells) |

| Ocelot Aggro, Death and Taxes | 2 Pyroclasm; cut Force of Negation |

Against creature decks, Force of Negation is the usual cut. Against combo, cut Uro or Dryad.

**Honest odds**
With no mulligans and no Brainstorm/Ponder digging counted, the chance of drawing Scapeshift by turn 5 is about 57%. Drawing Omen, Dryad or Pact is about 72%, and both together about 40%. Ponder and Brainstorm improve that in real games, but this is a turn-4 or 5 combo in a format where some decks win faster. Treat it as a fun, real deck to play, not a proven top-tier one.

- **Damage math:** the 6-trigger count with Omen and the rule that Valakut counts *itself* entering are my reading of the card text. The tools didn't confirm them as rulings.
- **Blood Moon:** it would turn off Valakut's ability. I didn't look this up, so I'm only listing it as a risk; Force of Vigor is the answer.

I built **Weirding Worship**, a blue-white control brew around Zur's Weirding. The deck passed the legality check with no errors or warnings, and the submission was accepted.

**The plan:** Zur's Weirding reveals both hands. Whenever a player would draw, the other player may pay 2 life to send that card to the graveyard instead. Win on life and you control every draw the opponent gets: you bin their good cards and their hand is never hidden. Counters stop what's already in their hand, and Exalted Angel finishes the game.

**Why the key cards**
- **4 Zur's Weirding.** It's the engine. On its own you have a 60% chance to draw one by turn 6 on the play. 4 Impulse and 3 Fact or Fiction dig for it on top of that.
- **3 Words of Worship.** "{1}: The next time you would draw a card this turn, you gain 5 life instead." Use it on your own draw and the opponent never gets the chance to deny it. You gain 5 life and pay 2 to deny their draw, so you come out 3 life ahead every turn cycle. It only shows up in 3 recent lists, including one Parfait list that also played Zur's Weirding.
- **Impulse and Fact or Fiction.** Neither card counts as a draw: Impulse looks at cards and Fact or Fiction reveals them. Under your own Weirding, they're how you get cards the opponent can't deny.
- **Extra life:** Exalted Angel (gains life equal to its damage), Absorb (counter plus 3 life) and 2 Ivory Tower. Ivory Tower gains you life for each card in hand over 4, which suits a deck that holds counters and digs a lot. Counting Words of Worship, you have a 93% chance to see at least one life source by turn 6.
- **Interaction:** 4 Swords to Plowshares, 4 Counterspell, 2 Absorb, 2 Mana Leak, 2 Wrath of God.
- **Finishers:** 4 Exalted Angel and 2 Decree of Justice. Decree can be cycled at the end of the opponent's turn to make Soldier tokens.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern deck built around Squandered Resources and Natural Balance.
results.text:
I've built and submitted a BG Squandered Resources / Natural Balance deck for Premodern. It's a brew: neither card shows up in any Premodern list from the last 90 days, so there was no proven version to copy.

## The plan
Squandered Resources lets each land make mana twice: tap it, then sacrifice it for one more. Natural Balance then gives you 5 new basics, and they come in untapped because the card doesn't say "tapped." Here's a typical turn 3: tap 3 lands and an Elf, then sacrifice the 3 lands, for 7 mana. Cast Natural Balance from zero lands and fetch 5 Swamps. Tap them and sacrifice them for 10 more. That's about 13 mana, nearly all black, for a Drain Life of about 11 damage plus that much life. You can also keep the 5 Swamps, Drain for less, and finish next turn. A second Natural Balance gains about 6 more mana each time, but it needs GG, so fetch a couple of Forests the first time.

## Key cards
- **4 Squandered Resources, 4 Natural Balance:** the engine. Natural Balance only fetches if you have 4 or fewer lands, so the deck adds mana with **4 Llanowar Elves and 3 Birds of Paradise** rather than extra land drops.
- **4 Drain Life:** the finisher. It only takes black mana for X, which is why Natural Balance mostly fetches Swamps. It's also removal in a pinch.
- **4 Sylvan Library, 1 Skeletal Scrying, 2 Krosan Tusker:** card selection to find the pieces. Lands you sacrifice fill your graveyard, which feeds Skeletal Scrying. Drain Life's lifegain pays for Library's 4-life draws.
- **2 Spiritmonger, 2 Pernicious Deed:** big mana sinks for when you don't have Drain Life. Deed with a huge X clears the board, but it also destroys your own Squandered Resources and Sylvan Library if X is 2 or more.
- **4 Duress, 3 Smother:** cheap interaction, borrowed from Rock lists.

## Mana
23 lands: 9 Forest, 8 Swamp, 4 Llanowar Wastes, 1 Cabal Coffers, 1 Lake of the Dead. That's 17 basics for Natural Balance to find. With 5 fetched Swamps, Cabal Coffers turns 2 mana into 5, and Lake of the Dead sacrifices a Swamp for BBBB. The deck check passed with no warnings against Rock's mana base (about 12 black and 15 green sources). I run fewer lands than Rock (23 against their average of 24.6) because the dorks make up the difference.

## Sideboarding against the current field
- **Enchantress (12.5%):** +2 Naturalize, +1 Pernicious Deed, +2 Cabal Therapy. Take out Smother.
- **Terrageddon (11.2%):** Natural Balance already rebuilds you after Armageddon. You can also sacrifice lands with Squandered in response for one last burst of mana. +2 Diabolic Edict.
- **Stiflenought (10.4%):** +2 Diabolic Edict, +2 Cabal Therapy. Smother kills Dreadnought (mana value 1). Take out Spiritmonger and Deed.
- **Sligh / Goblins:** +3 Engineered Plague (name Goblin), +2 Ravenous Baloth. Take out Duress and Sylvan Library.
- **Hermit Druid / Replenish / Psychatog:** +3 Tormod's Crypt, +2 Cabal Therapy. Take out Spiritmonger, Tusker and Deed.

## Honest odds and caveats
- **Assembly is slow.** With no mulligans and no card selection, you have both Squandered Resources and Natural Balance by turn 4 on the play only 26.5% of the time. You have Squandered, Natural Balance and Drain Life all together by turn 5 on the draw 19.6% of the time. Sylvan Library and the cyclers help, but this is a midrange deck with a combo finish, not a reliable fast kill.
- **Natural Balance is symmetric.** An opponent with 4 or fewer lands also gets to fetch basics. Cast it when you gain more than they do.
- **Going all-in leaves you with zero lands.** Only sacrifice everything when Drain Life is lethal.
- **Not verified:** the mana totals above are my own arithmetic, not tool output. Do the whole sequence in one main phase so no floating mana is lost.

I built **UW Millstill**, a mill deck that runs on a Standstill control shell. It's a brew: Millstone, Traumatize and Ambassador Laquatus show 0 recent Premodern lists, so this hasn't been tested in events.

**The plan**
You play a normal UW control game with counters, Swords and Wrath. Instead of attacking with creatures, you mill. Millstone and Laquatus take 2–3 cards a turn at instant speed. Traumatize takes half their remaining library in one shot. Brain Freeze, cast at the end of their turn after a few other spells, finishes them off.

**Why these cards**
- **Millstone (4) + Standstill (3):** This is the core combo. Standstill only triggers when someone *casts a spell*. Using Millstone, Laquatus, Mishra's Factory or Faerie Conclave isn't casting, so you can lock the board with Standstill and keep milling. If the opponent breaks it, you draw three.
- **Ambassador Laquatus (2):** Pay {3} to mill 3 at instant speed. It's a second repeatable mill source and a 1/3 blocker. It's legendary, so only 2.
- **Traumatize (2):** Your big swing. Midgame it usually takes 15–20 cards. Only 2 because it costs 5 and is one-shot.
- **Brain Freeze (3):** Each copy mills 3. Cast at the end of their turn after an Impulse or a counter, it takes 6–9 cards. Real lists already run it: it shows up in 385 recent lists, mostly Stiflenought.
- **Shell from Standstill decks:** 4 Counterspell, 3 Mana Leak, 1 Prohibit, 4 Swords, 2 Wrath, 1 Powder Keg, 1 Disenchant, 4 Impulse, 2 Fact or Fiction. Force of Will and Brainstorm are banned in Premodern, so they're not in the deck.
- You'll have Millstone or Laquatus by turn 5 about 72% of the time on the play, before counting Impulse.

**The mana**
24 lands: 4 Flooded Strand, 4 Adarkar Wastes, 1 Coastal Tower, 7 Island, 4 Plains, 2 Mishra's Factory, 1 Faerie Conclave, 1 Dust Bowl. That gives 17 blue and 13 white sources, close to real Standstill lists. Those lists run 26 lands because their lands are their win conditions. This deck wins with cheap spells, so 24 is enough. The Factories are mainly blockers that don't break Standstill.

**Sideboarding**
- **Sligh / Goblins:** Bring in 2 Hydroblast, 2 Blue Elemental Blast, Circle of Protection: Red and Exalted Angel. Take out Traumatize, Brain Freeze and Prohibit if needed. Keep Powder Keg and both Wraths.
- **Enchantress (the most-played deck, 12.5%):** Bring in 2 Annul, 1 Disenchant and 2 Meddling Mage. Mill is good here because they draw a lot of cards. Take out Swords and Powder Keg.
- **Terrageddon:** Bring in 2 Teferi's Response and Meddling Mage (name Armageddon). Keep your lands back to protect against Armageddon.
- **Stiflenought:** Bring in Annul (Phyrexian Dreadnought is an artifact) and the blue blasts if their list is red. Keep Powder Keg for Dreadnought.
- **Hermit Druid, UB Psychatog, Replenish:** Bring in 2 Tormod's Crypt. **Warning:** milling these decks fills their graveyard, which helps them. Here, use Millstone carefully, and save Traumatize until you can clear their graveyard afterward or the game is already won.

**What I couldn't check**
- I don't have match results for this exact deck.
- I'm not sure what colors Terrageddon and Stiflenought run, so the red-blast plan against them is my guess.
- With an expected win around turn 10, this is a slow deck. Expect long matches and be careful with the round clock.

results.prompt: Brew me a Premodern control deck built around Nether Spirit.
results.text:
I built you a mono-black brew around Nether Spirit. I call it **Pestilence Spirit**.

**The plan**
Nether Spirit is your only creature, so the downsides of your own sweepers and sacrifice effects mostly fall on the opponent. Pestilence, Mutilate, Innocent Blood and your edicts clear their board. Spirit keeps coming back: at the start of your turn, if it's the only creature card in your graveyard, you may return it. You win with chip damage from Spirit and Mishra's Factory, Pestilence damage to both players, and Corrupt, powered by Cabal Coffers.

**Why these cards**
- **Pestilence (3) and Mutilate (2):** These are your board wipes. Pestilence is sacrificed at end of turn if no creatures are left, and Spirit is the creature that keeps it around. If Spirit dies to its own Pestilence, it's back next turn. Neither card has appeared in recent Premodern results, which is part of why this is a brew.
- **Sacrifice effects that cost you nothing:** Innocent Blood makes each player sacrifice a creature, so you give up Spirit and they lose a real one. Cabal Therapy's flashback cost is sacrificing a creature. Skulltap sacrifices a creature to draw two. With Spirit, all of these are free.
- **Diabolic Edict (4), Smother (2), Snuff Out (2):** Edicts are your answer to Stiflenought's Phyrexian Dreadnought. Snuff Out can be cast for 4 life instead of mana, but it only hits nonblack creatures.
- **Skeletal Scrying (2):** This is the most important card to understand. If two Spirits are in your graveyard, neither one comes back. Scrying exiles cards from your graveyard to draw that many, so it gets rid of the extra Spirit and refills your hand.
- **Phyrexian Arena (3), Duress (4), Cabal Therapy (4):** card draw and hand disruption, borrowed from the Moneyball Black shell.

**The mana**
The deck runs 24 lands: 19 Swamp, 2 Mishra's Factory, 2 Wasteland and 1 Cabal Coffers, for 20 black sources. Real Moneyball Black lists average about 23 lands and 17 black sources. I went one land higher for the 4-drops, Corrupt and Coffers, and kept almost all the lands Swamps because Mutilate, Corrupt and Coffers all count Swamps. The deck check passed with no warnings.

**Sideboarding against the current meta**
- **Enchantress (12.5%) and Replenish:** bring in Dystopia ×3 and Gloom ×2, and use Wasteland on Serra's Sanctum. Take out the Smothers and some edicts. Add Tormod's Crypt against Replenish.
- **Sligh and Goblins:** bring in Engineered Plague ×3 and Vendetta ×2, and maybe Powder Keg. Take out Skulltap and Phyrexian Arena, because you'll be short on life.
- **Stiflenought:** you're already well set up with edicts. Bring in Powder Keg for their small creatures and take out Mutilate.
- **Hermit Druid Combo and UB Psychatog:** bring in Tormod's Crypt ×3 and Haunting Echoes. Take out Mutilate and Smother.
- **Terrageddon:** keep up Snuff Out and edicts for Terravore. Take out Engineered Plague effects if you brought them in.

**Honest odds and caveats**
- **Spirit doesn't come fast.** With 4 copies, you see one by turn 5 only 56.6% of the time. You see a sweeper by then 65.1% of the time, and both together only 35.5%. The deck can play the first few turns as pure discard and removal, so this is usually fine.
- **There's already a Nether Spirit deck.** Contamination plays it with Pernicious Deed and Zombie Infestation. I deliberately went a different direction, but that list is the proven alternative if you'd rather have it.
- **Watch your life total.** Pestilence, Arena, Snuff Out and Skeletal Scrying all cost you life, and only Corrupt gains it back.
- **This hasn't been tested.** The synergies come straight from the cards' rules text, but how the deck does in actual games is a guess.
